title: Probe asset deprecation and redistribution playbook
author: Sofia Ramirez
content:
Overview
========

This playbook defines Redwood Inference's standardized process for deprecating, archiving, and redistributing probe assets (prompts, annotated examples, synthetic probes, and associated telemetry) used across the eval harness, onboarding flows, and quality guardrails. It ensures probe inventory evolves without losing provenance, enables safe reuse across workloads, and reduces annotation debt while protecting reproducibility for past evaluations and regression triage.

Why this matters
-----------------
- Probe inventory grows quickly; stale probes reduce evaluation signal-to-noise and increase annotation cost.
- Unmanaged deletion risks losing reproducibility for past rollouts and impedes regression investigations.
- Controlled redistribution (re-use) can accelerate cold-start evaluation for new services and quantization experiments without duplicating annotation effort.

Scope
-----
Applies to: prompt sets, adversarial probes, synthetic-generated probes, human-annotated labels, probe metadata (fingerprints, schema), and canonical priming templates stored in the probe registry.
Not in scope: production traffic logs, raw customer PII datasets, and third-party licensed datasets covered by external contracts (see Data Governance).

Definitions
-----------
- Probe asset: any input example, prompt template, or synthetic seed used by the eval harness.
- Active probe: currently in a production eval suite, scheduled probe rotation, or onboarding checklist.
- Dormant probe: not scheduled for active evaluation in > 90 days but retained for provenance.
- Deprecated probe: flagged for removal from active usage and scheduled for archival after a cooling period.
- Redistribution: reassigning a deprecated/dormant probe into a new collection, possibly with relabeling.

Roles & Ownership
-----------------
- Probe Owners: service product/ML engineers who register probes for their service. Responsible for nominations, deprecation justification, and relabel requests.
- Probe Steward: Applied ML team role that approves deprecation, tags lifecycle state, and orchestrates redistribution.
- Annotation Stewards: Labeling ops who own annotation retention and GDPR/PII checks.
- Eval Harness Team: ensures pipelines respect TTLs and can replay archived probes for regression triage.

Lifecycle policy (summary table)
-------------------------------
| Lifecycle state | Trigger | Retention | Annotation TTL | Access level | Notes |
| Active | In-schedule / tagged as critical | 180 days rolling | 540 days | Read/write to eval pipelines | Rotates per probe-rotation policy |
| Dormant | No schedule > 90 days | 365 days | 540 days | Read-only; flag for steward review | Candidate for redistribution |
| Deprecated -> Cooling | Owner or steward flags | 30-day cooling | 365 days | Read-only; archived in cold storage | Owners can appeal within cooling period |
| Archived | Post-cooling | 1825 days (5 years) | 365 days or per legal | Restricted read | Audit logs retained; used for reproducing past evals |
| Purged | Legal retention met or explicit safe-delete | N/A | N/A | Deleted | Purge requires 2 approvals (Steward + Annotation Steward) |

Deprecation criteria
--------------------
A probe should be considered for deprecation when at least one of the following is true:
1) Low signal: failure rate vs. baseline < 1% across last 30-day eval window and low entropy in model responses.
2) Redundancy: semantic duplicate with >80% similarity to newer canonical probe family (use embedding clustering).
3) Annotation drift: labels consistently disagreed by >25% between annotator cohorts and correction cost high.
4) Contract/external constraint: licensing change or legal restriction that prohibits reuse.

Deprecation workflow (step-by-step)
-----------------------------------
1. Owner nominates probe(s) via probe-registry UI or CLI with deprecation_reason tag.
2. Probe Steward validates triggers (automated checks + manual review).
3. If accepted, probe enters Cooling state for 30 days and is labeled deprecated:{date}. During cooling:
   - The probe is excluded from default eval schedules but available to replay.
   - Annotation snapshots are taken and stored.
   - Owners notified and can appeal via the stewardship ticket.
4. After cooling, Steward either archives or redistributes. For archive: move to cold storage, set access restrictions and update provenance metadata. For redistribute: follow the Redistribution rules below.
5. If both Steward and Annotation Steward approve purge after legal TTL, execute erase and update audit log.

Redistribution rules and prioritization
--------------------------------------
Goal: re-use probes to seed new collections and onboarding checks while maintaining balanced coverage and avoiding contamination of held-out evaluation sets.
Principles:
- Never reuse probe assets that were part of a held-out gold standard for a live SLA without explicit re-ratification.
- Prioritize redistribution to:
  a) low-resource language campaigns,
  b) function-call and multimodal priming suites,
  c) cold-start onboarding bundles for new customer-facing services.
- When redistributing: assign a new probe_id, append original_probe provenance tag, and create a redistribution_record containing rationale, owner, and relabel requirements.

Redistribution prioritization matrix (text)
- Priority 1: Low-resource languages + high annotation quality (>=90% annotator agreement)
- Priority 2: Functioncall/structure probes with deterministic outputs
- Priority 3: Generic prompts useful for warmup or baseline calibration
- Priority 4: Adversarial probes retained for stress-testing but with known labels

Relabeling and annotation policy for redistributed assets
------------------------------------------------------
- Any redistributed probe that changes evaluation context must be relabeled by a fresh annotation pass (minimum N=3 annotators) and pass agreement threshold of 75% before being included in a production eval set.
- For quantization or model-variant testing where label fuzziness is acceptable, use a label-confidence bucket and mark the probe as soft-labeled. Soft-labeled probes must not be used for pass/fail quality gates.

Integration points with other systems
------------------------------------
- Eval harness: pipelines must respect lifecycle labels. Archived probes are excluded from daily schedules by default but available for targeted backfills and regression replay.
- Model onboarding: onboarding checklist must include probe provenance checks and a step to flag candidate reused probes for relabeling.
- Quant profiles: Redistribution records must include quant-sensitivity metadata (e.g., tokens sensitive to 4-bit vs 8-bit rounding). This helps the Optimize team choose safe reuse candidates.
- Regression triage: Archived probes act as canonical evidence for past releases. When triaging regressions, the triage runbook will include re-running archived probe bundles before suspecting model change.

Operational runbook (play-by-play)
---------------------------------
1) Incident: model regression suspected on Production Route A.
   - Pager triggers: SLI degradation > 5% or response quality fail rate increase > 2x baseline.
   - Eval harness oncall runs archived-bundle-replay script to compare current outputs with archived golden outputs. Example command:
     ./eval-harness replay --bundle archived/probes/service-A/2025-10 --compare --metrics coherence,answer-stability
2) If regression reproduces on archived bundle -> open regression huntbook with probe provenance attached.
3) If regression does not reproduce -> escalate to orchestration/serving runtime team for capacity/kv-cache investigation.

Example CLI snippets and YAML manifest
-------------------------------------
# Deprecate probes via CLI
# probe-registry deprecate --probe-id prb_02341 --reason "redundant-with-new-template-2026" --owner "service-search"

# Redistribution manifest (YAML)
redistribution_id: redist_2026_09
original_probe_ids: ["prb_02341", "prb_04502"]
destination_collections: ["cold-start-onboarding/en-us", "multimodal/priming"]
relabel_required: true
relabel_instructions: "3 annotators, majority vote. If <75% agreement, mark soft-labeled."
quant_sensitivity_tags: ["sensitive-4bit", "token-locality-high"]
provenance: "original_registry:2024-10; steward:Sofia-Ramirez"

Metrics, alerting & audit
-------------------------
- Key metrics to track: probe-utilization-rate, probe-redundancy-index (embedding-cluster density), annotation-agreement, redistribution-success-rate.
- Automated alerts:
  - probe-utilization < 0.5% for 90 days -> auto-tag dormant
  - redistribution without relabel flag -> fail pipeline and alert Steward
- Audit requirements: every state transition (active -> dormant -> deprecated -> archived -> purged) must append a signed audit entry with timestamp and actor. Audit entries are immutable and retained per retention policy.

Quantization and KV-cache considerations
---------------------------------------
- Redistributed probes must carry a quant-compatibility hint produced by the Quant Profiles team. For example: safe_in_4bit: false, expected_rounding_noise: low.
- Probes that exercise long-context KV-cache warmup should be tagged "kv-warmup" and are prioritized for mixed-precision stress tests before being included in quant-sensitive evals.

Security and privacy checks
--------------------------
- Annotation Stewards run a PII scanner on any probe before redistribution. If PII is detected but redaction is possible, create a redaction record and require a second annotation pass.
- Any probe with customer-identifiable content requires legal sign-off prior to reuse outside original service boundary.

Escaping common failure modes (lessons learned)
---------------------------------------------
- Failure: accidental inclusion of archived gold set in a public benchmark. Mitigation: enforce collection-level flags and pipeline gate that rejects archived-tagged probes from public export jobs.
- Failure: redistribution caused leakage into held-out evaluation set. Mitigation: require lineage check when adding probes to any dataset used in SLA evaluation; cross-check embedding similarity to gold sets.

Appendix: quick reference tables
--------------------------------
Retention and access quick reference
- Active: Rolling 180 days, open access to pipelines.
- Dormant: 365 days, read-only.
- Cooling/Deprecated: 30 days, owner appeal window.
- Archived: 5 years, restricted access; audit log plus snapshot of annotations.
- Purged: after legal TTL and 2 approvals.

Required approvals matrix
- Archive action: Probe Steward + Service Owner
- Purge action: Probe Steward + Annotation Steward + Legal (if PII/contracted)
- Redistribution into SLA-gold collections: Probe Steward + Product Owner + Eval Lead
